runs.text: Read three sides, in whole centimetres, and show
if they are all different, or
if those sides cannot make one. A triangle can be made when each side is less than the sum of the other two.

hints.text: Build a decision table: which questions do you need to ask, and which cases tell them apart?
There is a question that goes before all the others: if it is not a triangle, it makes no sense to ask how many sides are equal.
For isosceles, any pair of equal sides will do: there are three possible pairs.
